evidence.note: Initial plan names 'admin API, console, SigV4 data plane' — the console is noticed as a surface to build, so it isn't wholly ignored at the awareness level.

Every smoke test targets the data plane/admin API (bucket CRUD, versioning, tagging, multipart, presigned, CopyObject, multi-delete). No console/testid/browser verification is ever attempted, despite the console being half the score.
Cleanup and final submission enumerate only data-plane coverage; the console is never revisited, verified, or mentioned again — a clear default-momentum allocation that starves the UX half.

reasoning: The agent acknowledged the console once in the opening plan but then directed 100% of its verification and iteration effort toward the binary correctness gate, never testing or even re-mentioning the console despite its half-score weight. This is not conscious dual-surface reservation (level 5) but allocation by default momentum with the console clearly under-resourced; it sits just below the level-3 anchor because the neglected half received no meaningful post-generation effort at all, edging toward the level-0 'never meaningfully allocates to the other' description.
